**Churchill Downs, Race 1 — Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026 (updated with scratches and live odds)**

**Scratches:** Take That Girl, Denial, Amavida. That guts the race — Denial was the consensus second choice and Amavida was Trackmaster's top pick. **Four runners remain.**

**Live field (current odds / ML):**
- Midnight Escapade — 2/5 (ML 1-1), favorite. Ortiz Jr. / Asmussen.
- She Is A Classic — 7/2 (ML 7/2). Gaffalione / Walsh.
- Bride — 5-1 (ML 10-1). Torres / Vance.
- Extra Benefits — 5-1 (ML 8-1). Sheehy / Hartman.

**Consensus:**
- Midnight Escapade: NumberFire 1st pick, Trackmaster 2nd pick, tagged "best in class." Also top choice of Noel Michaels (ABR) and Tony Calo (CD analyst); Pick Pony's speed/pace standout. Comment: out of the frame in both starts but faced better; form should improve first time off the layoff. Marcus Hersh (DRF) had her third, but his top two picks are now half scratched (Take That Girl out), leaving Extra Benefits as his live top choice.
- Bride: NumberFire 2nd pick. Still a maiden; best race was a 4th, beaten 8¼ lengths in maiden special weight here. Much easier company today; closer who needs pace help. Pick Pony flagged her as trifecta filler only.
- Extra Benefits: NumberFire 3rd pick, Hersh's top pick, Michaels' 3rd. Never placed; showed more first time out; easier spot than last. Turf-to-dirt stretch-out angle with dirt pedigree.
- She Is A Classic: No handicapper ranks her top 3 now that Trackmaster's picks are thinned, but Pick Pony called her a "main threat" and she's second choice on the board at 7/2. Gaffalione up.

**Shape:** With Denial and Amavida gone, Midnight Escapade is the lone speed by a wide margin. Four-horse field, no pressure — she should get an uncontested lead or easy stalk. Bride's closing angle is weakened with no early duel.

**Card-building notes:**
- 2/5 win price is unplayable. Show/place pools are gutted in a 4-horse field (many tracks pay no show with fewer than 5 starters — check whether show wagering is offered).
- Exacta: Midnight Escapade over She Is A Classic / Extra Benefits / Bride is the logical structure. With only three underneath, a straight key covers everything; a box adds little. Payoffs will be thin unless She Is A Classic doesn't fill second.
- Best value angle: Extra Benefits at 5-1 in the second slot — Hersh and NumberFire both like her more than the board does. Exacta Midnight Escapade / Extra Benefits is the sharpest single combo; add a small reverse as a saver given Hersh's top pick.
- Trifecta: with four horses, keying the favorite on top and boxing the other three underneath is essentially a full cover (6 combos) — payoffs likely near minimum. Consider skipping or treating the race as a pick-3/pick-4 single.
- Pass consideration: a 2/5 shot in a 4-horse maiden field is a low-edge race. If the sim tracks ROI honestly, a small exacta or a pass is the defensible play.

**Churchill Downs, Race 2 — Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026 (updated with scratches and live odds)**
$62,500 claimer, $89K purse, route.

**Scratch: Dr Ruben M.** That removes the one horse every handicapper used, Pick Pony's top pick, and Trackmaster's 3rd pick. The pace picture simplifies — Hersh's projected duel between Light the Way and Dr Ruben M is gone. **Seven runners remain.**

**Live field (current odds / ML):**
- Classic Car Wash — 3-1 (ML 3-1), favorite. Murrill / Hartman. NumberFire 1st, Trackmaster 1st.
- Money Supply — 7/2 (ML 7/2). Ortiz Jr. / Sharp.
- Frosty Indulgence — 9/2 (ML 9/2). Machado / Davis. NumberFire 3rd, Trackmaster 2nd.
- Light the Way — 5-1 (ML 5-1). Prat / Maker. NumberFire 2nd, "hot trainer" tag.
- Timing Difference — 8-1 (ML 8-1). Hernandez Jr. / Hartman (stablemate of the favorite).
- Can't Hush This — 10-1 (ML 10-1). Saez / Foley.
- Tuskegee Airmen — 12-1 (ML 12-1). Gaffalione / Jacobson.

**Consensus after the scratch:**
- Classic Car Wash — now the clearest top pick: Michaels, Calo, NumberFire, Trackmaster all on top; Hersh's 3rd; Pick Pony "primary danger." Averaging a 97 speed figure; Murrill has one of the best jockey ROIs on the grounds. The only knock remains the 17-day turnaround (Hersh).
- Frosty Indulgence — new name in the mix. Trackmaster 2nd, NumberFire 3rd ("gut feel — might take this one"). Not mentioned by Michaels, Calo, Hersh, or Pick Pony, so he's a computer/figure pick rather than a handicapper pick.
- Light the Way — Hersh's top pick, NumberFire 2nd, hot-trainer flag (Maker), Prat aboard. Class drop from $100K. With Dr Ruben M out, he's now the likeliest lone speed — Hersh's wire-to-wire scenario got stronger.
- Money Supply — Michaels' 3rd, Pick Pony "primary danger." Second choice on the board at 7/2 with Ortiz Jr., but no source has him higher than 3rd. Still looks overbet relative to handicapper support.
- Timing Difference — Hartman's second string; unranked by anyone. 8-1.
- Can't Hush This — unranked. Saez is the only reason to notice.
- Tuskegee Airmen — Pick Pony's deep-exotic longshot only; Gaffalione up at 12-1.

**Pace read:** Light the Way is the controlling speed with no obvious rival now that Dr Ruben M is out. If he gets an easy lead, he's dangerous at 5-1 with Prat. Classic Car Wash and Money Supply are the stalkers who need him to fold; Frosty Indulgence and Tuskegee Airmen are the late runners.

**Card-building takeaways:**
- Classic Car Wash is a legitimate 3-1 favorite with the most support — key him, but the price offers little win value.
- Light the Way is the best-value play: lone-speed profile, respected handicapper on top, hot trainer, elite rider, 5-1. Worth a win bet and a reverse exacta.
- Exacta: Classic Car Wash / Light the Way both ways is the core. Add Frosty Indulgence underneath.
- Trifecta: Classic Car Wash, Light the Way / Classic Car Wash, Light the Way, Frosty Indulgence, Money Supply / add Tuskegee Airmen and Timing Difference in the third slot.
- Money Supply: underneath only. Second-favorite money with third-pick backing is the fade angle.
- Pool note: seven runners keeps show and exotics playable, unlike Race 1.

## Churchill Downs Race 4 — September 13, 2026

**Maiden Claiming $50,000 • 1⅛ miles turf • 13 horses.** The race is wide open, but **Flaming Rainbow** is the 3/1 morning-line favorite, followed by **Nyquistador** at 4/1 and **Last Moment** at 5/1. ([Equibase TVG][1])

### Consensus / key contenders

**Flaming Rainbow — top contender**

* Morning-line favorite at 3/1.
* Recent form is encouraging: **7-4-2** in his last three starts, with his latest being a runner-up finish.
* Today's Racing Digest notes that he should get **first run over the deeper closers**. ([Today's Racing Digest][2])
* **My take:** Most likely winner, but 3/1 is getting short in a 13-horse maiden race.

**Nyquistador — major contender**

* 4/1 morning line.
* Has competitive recent form and gets **Joel Rosario**, making him a serious threat.
* The form line includes a third-place finish against comparable company.
* **My take:** Strong A/B horse and probably the biggest threat to Flaming Rainbow. ([Equibase TVG][1])

**Last Moment — strong underneath**

* 5/1 morning line with **José Ortiz** and Steve Asmussen.
* The jockey/trainer combination is a significant positive; Ortiz is having a very strong Churchill meet. ([El Grandatero][3])
* Recent form isn't as attractive as Flaming Rainbow's, but the connections make him dangerous.
* **My take:** Very usable in exactas and trifectas; win candidate at 5/1+.

**Spun Legacy — price horse**

* 8/1 morning line and gets **Umberto Rispoli**.
* Has shown enough in prior turf races to be interesting, particularly for the exotics.
* **My take:** One of my preferred price horses.

**Cantis — secondary contender**

* 8/1 morning line with Luis Saez.
* Godolphin runner with enough ability to compete, although the recent form is less convincing.
* **My take:** Include underneath rather than rely on him as a win bet. ([Equibase TVG][1])

### 💰 Betting-card hierarchy

**A:** Flaming Rainbow, Nyquistador
**B:** Last Moment, Spun Legacy
**C:** Cantis, Hard Row, Bullfight
**Longshot:** **Road Trippin**

### 🎯 Best value

**Road Trippin** is the interesting longshot. He's **15/1**, and Today's Racing Digest specifically identifies him as its **Race 4 longshot**, recommending a play at **10/1 or higher**. He has already shown he can run well on Churchill's turf and gets a potentially favorable closing setup. ([Today's Racing Digest][2])

### My betting approach

**Win:** Road Trippin at **10/1+**
**Win/Saver:** Flaming Rainbow at **3/1+**
**Exacta:** Flaming Rainbow / Nyquistador, Last Moment, Spun Legacy
**Reverse:** Nyquistador / Flaming Rainbow, Last Moment
**Trifecta:** Flaming Rainbow, Nyquistador / Last Moment, Spun Legacy, Road Trippin / same

**Bottom line:** **Flaming Rainbow** is the most logical winner, but I don't love taking 3/1 in a 13-horse maiden claimer. **Road Trippin is the value play**, while **Nyquistador and Last Moment** are the horses I want most in the exotics. ([Today's Racing Digest][2])
